page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 614 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core capabilities are strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 2702.68, placing it in the top 25%. However, due to the low core count of 4 vCPUs, multi-core benchmarks are weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance (5400.57) and Geekbench multi-core score (3669.0). Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score and large-block read-only memory bandwidth (39.9 GB/sec) are average, the write bandwidth for large blocks (22.94 GB/sec) and read bandwidth for small cached blocks are weak.

This server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The high RAM density allows for large in-memory datasets, but the limited CPU core count makes it less suitable for heavy multi-threaded compute tasks, database operations (which scored in the bottom 25% on PassMark), or high-throughput web serving. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded data processing, memory-bound applications with low CPU concurrency requirements, and lightweight text or image processing tasks.
